yt-kissa.topic: Ep 12: Kavita reveals Meera really did leave that night to protect little Kabir from Vikram and hid with Ramesh Saxena's help, while Vikram's spy photographs Riya and Kavita together and sends the picture to Vikram
yt-kissa.why: Connects Ramesh, Meera and Vikram into one backstory, answers why Ramesh sent the box, and brings back Vikram's spy to raise the danger of exposure.

yt-kissa.topic: Ep 13: Vikram shows Dadi a doctored clip suggesting the marriage is fake, and Riya and Kabir must stage a convincing anniversary-style dinner to save the contract, only for Kabir's childhood friend Aarav to arrive and see through the act
yt-kissa.why: Escalates the no-one-finds-out rule under pressure, introduces the second lead properly and sets up a love triangle with a fun, romantic set piece.

yt-kissa.topic: Ep 14: Aarav promises to keep the secret but asks Riya to help him with a surprise for Kabir, and during a rainy bakery night Riya and Kabir almost kiss, breaking the no-feelings rule while Aarav watches from the doorway
yt-kissa.why: Delivers the first major romantic beat, breaks a rule and plants jealousy and tension between Kabir and Aarav for the middle of the season.

yt-kissa.topic: Ep 15: Kavita is found missing from her hideout, leaving only a torn page from Ramesh Saxena's old ledger showing a payment to someone inside the Malhotra mansion, so Riya realises the traitor may be a trusted family member, not just Vikram
yt-kissa.why: Reignites the mystery, widens the suspect pool and gives Riya a personal investigation that ties her father's debt to the family secret.

yt-kissa.topic: Ep 16: Riya secretly searches Vikram's study and finds the missing loan-waiver envelope, but Kabir catches her and, hurt that she broke his trust, accuses her of working against him, ending with Vikram locking them inside and calling Dadi
yt-kissa.why: Brings the missing envelope back as a major clue, creates a trust conflict between the leads and ends the arc on a high-stakes cliffhanger that moves the story toward the midseason confrontation.

yt-instinct.topic: Les corbeaux reconnaissent les visages humains et gardent rancune pendant des années (étude de l'université de Washington)
yt-instinct.why: Étude scientifique solide et histoire à tension narrative (vengeance, transmission aux autres corbeaux) ; mardi 07h IST (03h30 Paris, 21h30 Québec lundi) cible le public du soir au Québec.

yt-instinct.topic: La grenouille des bois qui gèle complètement en hiver, cœur arrêté, puis redevient vivante au printemps
yt-instinct.why: Hook fort « morte puis vivante », adaptation extrême bien sourcée (Rana sylvatica, glucose antigel) ; plaît aux familles et aux adultes, bon pour le visionnage en soirée au Québec.

yt-instinct.topic: Les éléphants s'appellent par des noms individuels, découverte publiée dans Nature Ecology & Evolution en 2024
yt-instinct.why: Actualité scientifique récente mais intemporelle, forte charge émotionnelle et partage facile ; mardi 11h IST (07h30 Paris) correspond au réveil et aux trajets matinaux en Europe.

yt-instinct.topic: Le tardigrade survit au vide spatial, à la radiation et à la déshydratation grâce à l'état de cryptobiose
yt-instinct.why: Sujet populaire, très bien documenté (expérience FOTON-M3 en 2007), curiosité élevée pour toutes les tranches d'âge ; mardi 13h IST (09h30 Paris) accroche la pause matinale européenne.

yt-instinct.topic: Le mimétisme du poulpe imitateur : il se fait passer pour une rascasse, un serpent de mer ou une méduse selon le danger
yt-instinct.why: Visuel spectaculaire adapté aux images stock et IA, histoire claire en trois transformations, rétention élevée ; mardi 15h IST (11h30 Paris, 05h30 Québec) vise la pause de midi européenne.

yt-hopeverse.topic: Slot Tue 27 Oct 07:00 IST (Indian viewers): Pick the top India morning-news story from 26-27 Oct 2026, such as a market move, a policy or court decision, or a cricket result. Name the specific event, the people involved and one number. It must not be the Jamia polls, the Rahul Gandhi-Puri-Epstein row, the Kharge 'baap' complaint or the Jio IPO, because those are already made or planned.
yt-hopeverse.why: A 07:00 IST slot suits a quick 'what you need to know today' Short. Search failed, so I could not verify a specific story and have not made one up. Before scripting, confirm the story and its date from a source such as PTI, The Hindu or Indian Express. Prefer a story with a clear number and a direct effect on viewers' day.

yt-hopeverse.topic: Jamia Millia Islamia agrees to hold student union polls after 21 years, ending a hunger strike. It revokes suspensions and orders a probe into security personnel conduct
yt-hopeverse.why: A campus story with a clear sequence of events and a '21 years' number. It suits the student-heavy Indian audience at 09:00 IST.

yt-hopeverse.topic: Rahul Gandhi asks 'which traitor is US blackmailing' and targets the BJP and RSS over the Puri-Epstein picture: what was said and how the parties responded
yt-hopeverse.why: Political rows get strong engagement from Indian viewers. A neutral explainer of the claim and the replies fits the 11:00 IST slot.

yt-hopeverse.topic: Bihar BJP worker files a police complaint at Patna's Kotwali station over Kharge's 'baap' remark aimed at Modi, filed Sunday evening: what he said and what the complaint means
yt-hopeverse.why: A fast-moving political story from the last 24 hours with a clear who and what. It suits the 13:00 IST slot, when Indian viewers are looking for the day's political updates.

yt-hopeverse.topic: Lula's win at 80: what a 4th term means for Brazil, BRICS and global politics, with the key facts in 60 seconds
yt-hopeverse.why: The 15:00 IST slot targets international viewers, and this is the biggest world story I found. I'd make it a different video from the 17:00 one, focused on the global impact (BRICS, trade, climate) and not the result itself. I could only pull a limited set of headlines, so check the angle against fresh reports before filming.
